children: Gorman-Rupp's board has raised the company's quarterly dividend by 5.3%, to 20 cents from 19 cents, making it 54 straight years that the maker of pumps and pumping systems has boosted its payout.
Gorman-Rupp's new quarterly rate, equal to 80 cents a year, represents an annual yield of about 1.14% based on Thursday's closing price of $70.13, up from 1.08%.

The increase maintains Gorman-Rupp's spot on the elite list of dividend kings: those who have boosted their dividends annually for at least 50 years. That group currently counts 60 members, according to website Sure Dividend.
The Mansfield, Ohio, company on Friday said the increased dividend is payable Dec. 10 to shareholders of record Nov. 13.
